"""Draft 2: a word-final German/Scandinavian/Dutch noun suffix (-ung, -ning, -ing, -ering...)
that completes a word, in a document whose text so far looks Germanic rather than English.
Such a suffix piece pushes the residual stream strongly negative; elsewhere it is 0."""

READS = ()

# Suffix pieces that close a deverbal noun, with the group's typical strength.
UNG_SUFFIXES = {"ung", "ungen", "ungs", "nung", "zung", "hung", "ziehung", "bindung", "ührung"}
ING_SUFFIXES = {"ning", "ningar", "ningen", "ninger", "nings", "ering", "ierung", "eling",
                "elling", "king", "ving", "else", "ing", "ings", "ingen", "arming", "ring"}

# Function words that mark the text as German/Scandinavian/Dutch, and as English.
GERMANIC = set("der die und ist nicht mit ein eine zu den von auf für dem das sich auch "
               "nach wir sie ich er es og det som med til af en et er ikke jeg för och att "
               "är av het een ik niet van voor je dat zijn oder aber sind werden wird".split())
ENGLISH = set("the and of is to that with for it this are be you on as was by at from or an "
              "which have".split())


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    """carry: (document id, Germanic word count, English word count) for the current document."""
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:
        carry = (doc, 0, 0)
    _, germanic, english = carry
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    word = token.strip().lower()
    value = 0.0
    if not token.startswith(" ") and word in UNG_SUFFIXES | ING_SUFFIXES:
        if germanic >= 2 and germanic > english:
            value = -2.2 if word in UNG_SUFFIXES else -3.0
    germanic += word in GERMANIC
    english += word in ENGLISH
    return (doc, germanic, english), value

"""Approximate a shell-argument punctuation detector.

Option-leading dashes after familiar commands get large negative responses.
Path, pipe, variable, and shell-test punctuation get smaller responses.
There are also fixed responses to script suffixes, soft hyphens, and an
initial Title: label. Everything else stays close to zero. Only a short
text suffix is retained, and it is cleared at document boundaries.
"""
import re

READS = ()
FILE_TOOLS = frozenset('''
cat grep egrep fgrep rg head tail sed awk curl wget cp mv rm
'''.split())
COMMANDS = FILE_TOOLS | frozenset('''
ls find mkdir rmdir ln chmod chown tar gzip gunzip zip unzip ssh scp rsync
ps kill du df wc sort uniq cut tr tee xargs env sudo su bash sh zsh
apt apt-get yum dnf pacman git hg svn python python3 pip pip3 npm npx yarn
pnpm node java javac go cargo rustc rustfmt make cmake gcc clang docker
kubectl pytest tox mvn gradle php phpunit dotnet timeout exec install
export diff ssh-keygen ssh-keyscan ssh-copy-id ffmpeg tsc ts-node jest
eslint webpack vite packer hdiutil ditto perl g++ set
'''.split())
SUBCOMMAND_TOOLS = frozenset('''
git hg svn go cargo npm npx yarn pnpm docker kubectl dotnet packer
hdiutil pip pip3 mvn
'''.split())
SUBCOMMANDS = frozenset('''
add apply attach detach cat-file uninstall bench branch build check checkout
clean clone commit config diff doc fetch fix fmt init install list log mod
pull push rebase remove reset restore run show start status switch test
update version
'''.split())
# These words alone, further back in prose, are weak evidence of a command.
AMBIGUOUS = frozenset('''
go make find install export head tail log ln sort set
'''.split())
RECENT_COMMANDS = COMMANDS - AMBIGUOUS
WORD = re.compile(r'[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_+-]*')
MARKERS = frozenset((
    ' -', ' --', ' /', ' ./', ' &&', ' |', ' $', ' "$', '.sh', '.py',
    '\xad', ':', '--', " '--", ' "--', ' `-', ' [-', '="-', ' [',
))


def context(text):
    line = text.replace('\\\n', ' ').replace('\\n', '\n').rsplit('\n', 1)[-1]
    match = re.search(r'(?<![A-Za-z0-9_^])([A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_+-]*)$', line)
    last = match[1] if match else ''
    pair = re.search(r'([A-Za-z0-9-]+)[ \t]+([a-z][a-z-]*)$', line)
    subcommand = bool(pair and pair[1] in SUBCOMMAND_TOOLS
                      and pair[2] in SUBCOMMANDS)
    invocation = bool(re.search(
        r'''(?:^|["'`;&|])[ \t]*(?:find|make|set)(?:[ \t]|$)'''
        r'|\bgo (?:test|run|build)\b', line))
    recent = invocation or any(
        w in RECENT_COMMANDS for w in WORD.findall(line[-70:]))
    option = bool(re.search(r'[ \t]-{1,2}[A-Za-z]', line[-100:]))
    command = last in COMMANDS and (last != 'set' or invocation)
    return last, command, subcommand, invocation, recent, option


def predict(token, text):
    if token not in MARKERS:
        return -0.003
    last, command, subcommand, invocation, recent, option = context(text)
    if token in (' -', ' --'):
        if re.search(r'(?:if|elif|while)[ \t]+\[', text.rsplit('\n', 1)[-1]):
            return -2.9
        if last in FILE_TOOLS:
            return -5.0 if option else -4.65
        if command or subcommand:
            return -4.1 if token == ' --' else -3.9
        if re.search(r'''\.(?:py|sh|js|ts|rb|pl)["']?$''', text):
            return -3.3
        if invocation:
            return -3.1
        if recent:
            return -3.3 if option or token == ' --' else -1.0
        if option and token == ' --':
            return -2.5
        return -0.03 if token == ' -' else -0.2
    if token == ' [':
        return -2.5 if last in ('if', 'elif', 'while') else -0.003
    if token == ' /':
        if last == 'cd':
            return -1.97
        return -1.9 if command else -0.7 if recent else -0.1
    if token == ' ./':
        return -0.9
    if token == ' &&':
        return -1.1 if recent else -0.2
    if token == ' |':
        return -1.1 if recent and option else -0.6 if recent else 0.03
    if token in (' $', ' "$'):
        return -0.9 if recent or option or token == ' "$' else 0.0
    if token in (" '--", ' `-', ' [-'):
        return -1.0
    if token == ' "--':
        return -1.1 if recent or option else -0.1
    if token == '--':
        return -1.4 if text.endswith(('"', "'", '`')) else -0.02
    if token == '="-':
        return -2.2
    if token == '\xad':
        return -1.2
    if token == '.sh':
        return -0.88
    if token == '.py':
        return -0.29
    if token == ':' and text == 'Title':
        return -6.6876
    return -0.003


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    text = carry[1] if carry is not None and carry[0] == doc else ''
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    return (doc, (text + token)[-160:]), predict(token, text)

"""Command-line option detector for layers.1.mlp.down_proj:3266.

What it does
------------
This component is a negative-going detector for option flags typed inside
shell commands. It tracks the current line of text (the carry holds it):

* A line is a shell line if it mentions a common command-line tool (grep,
  find, git, npm, cargo, pytest, kubectl, ...) or is a bash tool call (it
  contains "command").
* In a shell line, the space-hyphen that opens an option is strongly negative.
  A short option " -" right after a tool name (`grep -n`, `head -10`,
  `tail -20`) gives about -4.7. Other short options give about -2, and long
  options " --" give about -3.5 (`git checkout --`, `pytest -x --`).
* In a shell line, a path start (" /", " ./") and pipes or chains (" |",
  " &&", " >") are mildly negative (-1).
* Outside shell lines a bare " --" is mildly negative (-1). " -" is about 0
  there, since it is mostly a prose dash.
* A "Title:" colon at the start of a document (right after <|endoftext|>) is
  strongly negative (-6.5).
Everything else predicts 0.

What it leaves out: the spread within options (some `grep -` are -7, others
-1, and a few prose dashes in shell-looking lines are off), and weak effects on
ordinary words. A per-token table would add little, because whether the line is
a command carries most of the signal.
"""

import re

READS = ()

COMMAND_TOOLS = (
    "grep find cd git npm npx yarn cargo go python python3 pytest pip make docker "
    "kubectl ls cat head tail sed awk curl wget sudo apt php java mvn node rustc gcc "
    "tsc jest echo mkdir rm cp mv export timeout diff sort xargs cut tcpdump "
    "snmpwalk nyc mocha prettier eslint ssh scp rsync tar gunzip kill phpunit bundle"
).split()
TOOL_SET = set(COMMAND_TOOLS)
SHELL_LINE = re.compile(r"\b(?:" + "|".join(COMMAND_TOOLS) + r")\b|\"command\"")
SHORT_OPTION = {" -"}
LONG_OPTION = {" --", "'--"}
PATH_TOKENS = {" /", " ./"}
JOIN_TOKENS = {" |", " &&", " >"}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    previous = prefix.token_strings[-2] if len(prefix.token_strings) > 1 else ""
    new_document = len(prefix.document_ids) < 2 or (
        prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]
    )
    line = "" if carry is None or new_document else carry
    line = (token.split("\n")[-1] if "\n" in token else line + token)[-300:]

    if token == ":" and previous == "Title" and prefix.token_strings[-3:-2] == ["<|endoftext|>"]:
        return line, -6.5
    in_shell = bool(SHELL_LINE.search(line))
    if token in SHORT_OPTION or token in LONG_OPTION:
        if not in_shell:
            return line, (-1.0 if token in LONG_OPTION else 0.0)
        if previous.strip() in TOOL_SET and token in SHORT_OPTION:
            return line, -4.7
        return line, (-3.5 if token in LONG_OPTION else -2.0)
    if in_shell and (token in PATH_TOKENS or token in JOIN_TOKENS):
        return line, -1.0
    return line, 0.0

"""Layer 1 MLP down-projection, component 3267 (one rank-one piece of that matrix).

Plain-terms summary
-------------------
This component is nearly silent. Its activation is about +-0.05 at almost every
token, and nearly all of its large values come from the first token of each
document. That token has no earlier text for attention to use, so the component
reads the token itself. A capitalised word written with no leading space ("The",
"I", "She", "Person") pushes the activation down to about -0.2. Any other first
token pushes it down a little, about -0.05.

Prediction rule
---------------
* First token of a document (also the first token of a row): -0.22 if it is a
  capitalised word with no leading space, otherwise -0.05.
* Every other token: 0.

Document boundaries are the places where the document id changes, as in the model,
so the rule restarts at each packed document.

What this simple rule misses: the rest of the variance is a diffuse, token-specific
effect with no concept behind it that we found (word tokens with small signed
means, code and CJK tokens with mixed signs). A per-token table would explain more,
about 7% of the variance at document starts and about 17% overall, but it would be
a list of token ids and is not included.
"""

READS = ()

CAPITAL_WORD_FIRST = -0.22
OTHER_FIRST = -0.05


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    t = prefix.position
    starts_document = t == 0 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]
    if not starts_document:
        return carry, 0.0
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    capital_word = token[:1].isupper() and token.isalpha()
    return carry, CAPITAL_WORD_FIRST if capital_word else OTHER_FIRST

"""Layer-1 MLP down_proj component 3268: a sparse 'modifier-slot' detector.

The component goes negative on the word that completes a place, nationality, language or
date modifier and sits in front of a head noun: "Berlin[-based]", "German[-born]",
"English[-language]", "Riverside [area]", "California [Native]", "Monday [morning]",
"New York [resident]", "无锡[区]". It also goes negative on "of" right after a unit or edition
noun ("the July 2012 issue [of]", "the 2019 edition [of]"). It is slightly positive on the
first token of a document. Everything else is near zero.
"""

READS = ()

# Hyphenated suffixes that attach to a place or nationality: "US-based", "German-born".
SUFFIXES = set("based born language speaking area".split())
# Category nouns that follow a place, nationality or name: "English language", "Bay area".
CATEGORY_NOUNS = set("language languages born native descent region zone market area office branch translation".split())
# Nouns for residents and citizens, which follow a place or nationality and usually
# lead into "of"/"in" phrases: "Michigan resident", "Dutch citizen".
PEOPLE_NOUNS = set("resident residents citizen".split())
# Time-of-day and time words after a day or a named period: "Friday night", "Monday morning".
TIME_NOUNS = set("time night morning afternoon".split())
# Nouns that name a unit, edition or part of something, and take "of" next.
EDITION_NOUNS = set("edition editions issue issues version episode season seasons division district borough branch chapter section region city country place town unit".split())
# Chinese administrative words (district, region) after a place name: "涪陵[区]".
CHINESE_AREA = set("区 地区 地區 區 県 市 本土".split())

SUFFIX_VALUE = -3.5
CATEGORY_VALUE = -0.7
PEOPLE_VALUE = -2.5
TIME_VALUE = -0.7
OF_VALUE = -0.7
CHINESE_VALUE = -1.5
DOC_START_VALUE = 0.1


def _is_proper(token):
    """A capitalised word, a number, a weekday or a CJK character: the kind of word a place
    or name ends in."""
    word = token.strip()
    if not word:
        return False
    if word[0].isupper() or word[0].isdigit():
        return True
    return "一" <= word[0] <= "鿿"


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    tokens = prefix.token_strings
    cur = tokens[-1]
    word = cur.strip().lower()
    same_doc = len(tokens) > 1 and prefix.document_ids[-2] == prefix.document_ids[-1]
    prev = tokens[-2] if same_doc else ""
    after_proper = _is_proper(prev)
    value = 0.0
    if cur.startswith("-") and word[1:] in SUFFIXES and after_proper:
        value = SUFFIX_VALUE
    elif cur == " of" and prev.strip().lower() in EDITION_NOUNS:
        value = OF_VALUE
    elif cur.strip() in CHINESE_AREA and after_proper:
        value = CHINESE_VALUE
    elif word in CATEGORY_NOUNS and after_proper:
        value = CATEGORY_VALUE
    elif word in PEOPLE_NOUNS and after_proper:
        value = PEOPLE_VALUE
    elif word in TIME_NOUNS and after_proper:
        value = TIME_VALUE
    elif not same_doc:
        value = DOC_START_VALUE
    return carry, float(value)

"""Personal pronouns. A layer-1 MLP feature that fires on personal pronouns in running text:
most strongly on the subject "I" (and "I'm", "I'd", "I've"), about 1.4x more inside quoted
speech, and growing as the document accumulates first-person pronouns. Weaker on "we", "me",
"my", "our", "us", "you", "your", and weaker still on "he", "she", "they", "them", "their",
"her". Also fires on escaped quote marks that open a string in code, and on Chinese and
French pronouns. Everything else predicts 0."""
READS = ()

QUOTES = {'"', "“", "”"}
FIRST_PERSON = {" I", "I", " me", "me", " my", "my", " we", " We", "We", " us", " our", "Our", " myself"}
VALUE = {
    # first person singular: the subject I, with its contractions
    " I": 0.85, "I": 0.45, "'m": 0.75, "’m": 0.8, "'d": 0.5, "’d": 0.7, "'ve": 0.4, "’ve": 0.45,
    "'ll": 0.3, "’ll": 0.4, "'re": 0.45, "’re": 0.45,
    # other first person
    " we": 0.4, " We": 0.45, "We": 0.4, " me": 0.35, " my": 0.5, "my": 0.25, " our": 0.5, "Our": 0.55,
    " us": 0.5, " myself": 0.45,
    # second person
    " you": 0.5, " You": 0.5, "You": 0.45, " your": 0.25, " Your": 0.3, " yourself": 0.4,
    # third person
    " they": 0.35, " They": 0.35, " them": 0.35, " their": 0.2, " he": 0.27, " He": 0.3,
    " him": 0.3, " she": 0.35, " She": 0.35, " her": 0.2,
    # escaped quote opening a string in code
    " \\\"": 0.8, "(\\\"": 0.7, "=\\\"": 1.3,
    # other languages
    "我": 0.7, "你": 0.7, "我们": 0.6, "您": 0.45, "你们": 0.9,
    " je": 0.3, " nous": 0.35, " vous": 0.3,
}
IN_QUOTE = 1.4  # pronouns inside quoted speech
FULL_AFTER = 4  # first-person pronouns seen in a document before the feature is at full strength


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    inside, last_doc, count = carry if carry else (False, None, 0)
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if doc != last_doc:  # a new document starts: reset the quote state and the count
        inside, count = False, 0
    tok = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    if tok in QUOTES:
        inside = not inside
    value = VALUE.get(tok, 0.0)
    if inside:
        value *= IN_QUOTE
    if tok in FIRST_PERSON:
        value *= 0.5 + 0.5 * min(count, FULL_AFTER) / FULL_AFTER
        count += 1
    return (inside, doc, count), value

READS = ()
"""Component layers.1.mlp.down_proj:3272 — a 'PHP' detector.

Its contribution is large (about +2.4) on the word "php" in any form that the
tokenizer splits off: ".php" file extensions, "/php", " PHP", " php", and above all
the "php" right after an opening "<?" tag (about +6). It is also a little positive on
the "<?" token itself. Everything else is small and noisy, except two cases:
  * the first token of every document (or of a packed row) sits at about -0.3, and
  * the two-character run "··" (repeated middle dots) sits at about -2.5.
Predicts those values and 0 elsewhere.
"""
import re

PHP_WORD = re.compile(r"^[./\- ]*php$", re.IGNORECASE)   # "php", ".php", " PHP", "-php"; not "PHPUnit"


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    if prefix.position == 0 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]:
        return None, -0.32                     # first token of a document
    if token == "··":
        return None, -2.5                      # run of middle dots
    if PHP_WORD.match(token):
        if prefix.token_strings[-2] == "<?":   # the "php" of "<?php"
            return None, 6.0
        return None, 2.4
    if token == "<?":
        return None, 2.0
    return None, 0.0

"""A lexical start-of-document signal, plus escaped/TeX backslashes.

At a document's first token, estimate a signed lexical score from word
frequency, length, case and dictionary word classes. Noun, verb and adjective
readings contribute different adjustments; these are dictionary possibilities,
not contextual part-of-speech tags. Later positions are near zero, except
double backslashes: positive in escaped strings, negative in recent TeX-like
context. This is a partial approximation, missing large word-specific effects.
No token-identity table is used.
"""
import math
import re
from functools import lru_cache
import wordnet
from wordfreq import zipf_frequency

READS = ()
FUNCTION_WORDS = set('''a an the and or but if as at by for from in into of
on onto out over than through to under up upon with without is am are was
were be been being have has had do does did not no can could will would may
might must shall should'''.split())
TEX = re.compile(
    r'\\(?:frac|sum|int|left|right|begin|end|alpha|beta|gamma|lambda|theta|'
    r'sigma|pi|over|hline|nonumber|qquad|quad|cdot|sqrt|color|text|eta|'
    r'epsilon|delta|omega|big|Big)'
)


@lru_cache(maxsize=16000)
def initial_score(s):
    w = s.strip()
    if s.startswith('<|'):
        return -.2
    if not w:
        return -.8 if len(s) > 1 and '\n' not in s else -.2
    if w.isdigit():
        return 0.
    if not any(c.isalpha() for c in w):
        return -.1

    # Word length, familiarity, and grammatical possibilities, not token IDs.
    key = w.strip('_./-#$')
    pos = wordnet.parts_of_speech(key) if key.isalpha() else set()
    cats = wordnet.categories(key) if key.isalpha() else set()
    frequency = zipf_frequency(key, 'en') if key.isalpha() else 0
    length = math.log1p(len(w))
    value = 1.03 + .44 * length - .26 * frequency
    value -= 1.05 * (frequency < 2)
    value += .37 * w.isupper() - .57 * w.istitle() - .66 * w.islower()
    value -= .23 * (len(w) == 1 and w.isalpha())
    value += .44 * (w.isupper() and len(w) > 1)  # acronyms
    value += .76 * w.startswith(('_', '/', '.'))  # code/path fragments
    value -= .11 * s.startswith(' ')
    value += .88 * (w.lower() in FUNCTION_WORDS)
    value += (.42 + .42 * length - .10 * frequency) * ('noun' in pos)
    value -= (.23 + .04 * frequency) * ('verb' in pos)
    value += (-1.66 + .21 * frequency) * ('adjective' in pos)
    value -= .20 * ('adverb' in pos)
    value += .53 * ('noun.artifact' in cats) + .61 * ('noun.animal' in cats)
    value += .40 * ('noun.plant' in cats) + .32 * ('noun.shape' in cats)
    value -= .34 * ('verb.cognition' in cats) + .44 * ('verb.change' in cats)
    return value


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    s = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    first = carry is None or carry[0] != doc
    recent = '' if first else carry[1]
    if first:
        value = initial_score(s)
    elif '\\\\' in s:
        if TEX.search(recent):
            value = -.8
        elif s.count('\\') > 2:
            value = .12
        else:
            value = .43
    elif s == 'cr' and recent.endswith('\\') and TEX.search(recent):
        value = -1.7
    else:
        value = .002
    return (doc, (recent + s)[-512:]), float(value)

"""layers.1.mlp.down_proj:3273 -- a "document-opening noun" detector.

What it does: this component is almost silent inside a document, but at the first token of
each document (the token after a document break, where attention cannot see anything before
it) it writes a value that depends on what kind of word that token is:
  - strongly positive for technology, computing, media and science words, and for acronyms,
    CamelCase identifiers and underscored names (LCD, VPN, Linux, API, DataManager, ...);
  - moderately positive for other nouns (common nouns, and words ending in noun suffixes
    such as -tion, -ment, -ness, -ity, -ics, -ware, -ism, -ogy, -er, -or);
  - negative for verbs, adjectives and adverbs (-ly, -ed, -ous, -ful, -ish, -ible, -ive, -less);
  - slightly negative for function words (the, of, to, my, ...);
  - near zero for punctuation, digits and everything else, and at all non-initial positions.

negative values. Additional rules cover 'use ... to', 'as ... as possible',
Japanese instrumental/location 'で', and middle-dot fillers. This is a coarse
phrase detector, not a parser. Keep only a bounded, document-local history.

    'manner': 'manner fashion',

    'form': 'form format',

    'basis': 'basis footing',

    'location': ('position direction location place space line level plane '
                 'coordinate background'),
    'state': 'state condition environment situation circumstance',
    'quantity': ('rate price cost speed temperature pace frequency quantity '
                 'amount number volume scale degree standard dose'),
    'time': ('time day week month year hour minute second period moment '
             'occasion interval stage night'),
}

                  'which what of').split())

    word = token.strip().lower()
    roots = {word}

    return word, tags, SIMPLIFY.convert(word)

    document = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    history = carry[1] if carry and carry[0] == document else ''
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    word, tags, chinese = classify(token)
    segment = re.split(r'[.,;:!?\n。！？；，]', history)[-1]
    words = re.findall('[A-Za-z]+', segment.lower())

        if previous in PREPOSITIONS:
            prep, distance = previous, j

                          segment[-80:], re.I))

                              ('time', .15), ('state', .23),

        for group, amount in (('manner', 1.22), ('form', .86),
                              ('wording', .55), ('location', .29)):

            value -= 1.53
        if distance >= 2 and 'way' in tags:
            value -= .76
    if prep == 'at' and distance <= 3:
        if 'quantity' in tags:

        if 'location' in tags:

"""Layer-1 MLP unit 3275 (down_proj), read from the text so far.

It goes negative on the word that closes a manner or measure phrase, the noun after a
preposition that says *how* or *under what condition* something happens:
  "in a timely MANNER", "in standard FORM", "on a regular BASIS", "in simple TERMS",
  "in a linear FASHION", "at low TEMPERATURES", "in any FORMAT".
Strongest for the manner nouns (manner, fashion, basis, mode, format); weaker for
measure and condition nouns (temperature, level, location, rate, time, years...)
and for a bare "way" or "method" that is not in such a phrase. In Chinese it goes
negative on a locative postposition (中, 内, 上, 下, 里) closing a 在...phrase
("在浏览器中", "在游戏内", "在根目录下"). Everywhere else it is 0.

The prediction is a hand-set table, not a fit: values are roughly the mean activation
of each word in its context, scaled to the component's units.
"""
import re

READS = ()

# How strongly each word pulls the unit negative when it closes a prepositional phrase.
MANNER = {"manner": -2.2, "fashion": -2.2, "basis": -1.5, "mode": -1.2, "format": -1.0,
          "temperatures": -1.2, "form": -0.6, "terms": -0.6, "conditions": -0.7,
          "way": -0.4, "approach": -0.3, "method": -0.3, "style": -0.3}
# Measure, place and time nouns: a weaker negative inside a prepositional phrase.
MEASURE = {"temperature", "level", "direction", "location", "environment", "language",
           "rate", "cost", "time", "position", "order", "years", "days", "scale"}
PREPS = {"in", "on", "at", "with", "under", "within"}
LOCATIVE = {"中", "内", "內", "上", "下", "里", "裡"}
PUNCT = re.compile(r"[^\w\s]")


def words_before(strings, k):
    """Up to k words before the current token, stopping at punctuation or a newline."""
    out = []
    for s in reversed(strings[:-1][-k:]):
        if PUNCT.search(s):
            break
        out.append(s.strip().lower())
    return out


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    s = prefix.token_strings
    word = s[-1].strip().lower()
    near_prep = any(w in PREPS for w in words_before(s, 4))
    if word in MANNER:
        # outside a prepositional phrase the same word is only weakly negative
        return carry, MANNER[word] * (1.0 if near_prep else 0.3)
    if word in MEASURE and near_prep:
        return carry, -0.3
    if s[-1].strip() in LOCATIVE and "在" in "".join(s[-9:-1]):
        return carry, -2.0
    return carry, 0.0

"""Layer-1 MLP down_proj, component 3276: a "this mark opens or closes text" detector.

Its activation is near 0 on most tokens. It is large on a few kinds of token, each
checked on training text:

- "Title:" that opens a document: the colon right after "Title" which follows
  <|endoftext|>. This is the largest activation seen (19.6), and always the same.
- A single bare space that starts an indented line, i.e. right after a line break.
  About 0.9 after a real newline and about 1.7 after an escaped newline ("\\n") inside a
  code string. A bare space right after an opening quote in a call, as in print(" or ('
  about 1.0 to 1.7.
- The end-of-thinking tag </think>: about 1.2.
- A full stop after a list number at the start of a line ("1.", "2.", "10."): about 0.8.
- A closing mark attached to a word, as in `name`, "word" or 'word': backtick 0.9,
  curly closing quote 0.7, straight double quote 0.5, apostrophe 0.25, bold or math
  closers 0.3.
- A bullet symbol ("-" or "•") at the start of a line: about 0.3.

Everything else predicts 0. The program is stateless: it reads only the last few tokens.
"""

import re

READS = ()

LINE_NUMBER_DOT = re.compile(r"(\n|\\n)\d+\.$")
OPEN_QUOTES = ('("', "('", '(\\"', ' "', '="', "'", '\\"')
CLOSE_AFTER_WORD = {"`": 0.9, "”": 0.7, '"': 0.5, "'": 0.25, "’": 0.2, "**": 0.3, "$$": 0.3}
LINE_BULLETS = {"-": 0.3, "•": 0.3}


def ends_line(text):
    # a real newline, or an escaped one as written inside code strings
    return text.endswith("\n") or text.endswith("\\n")


def is_word_end(s):
    # a token ending in a letter or digit: a mark after it is attached to a word
    return any(c.isalnum() for c in s) and not s[0].isspace()


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    strs = prefix.token_strings
    tok = strs[-1]
    prev = strs[-2] if len(prefix) > 1 else ""
    before = "".join(strs[-4:-1])  # the few tokens just before this one
    recent = "".join(strs[-6:-1])
    if tok == ":" and prev == "Title" and len(strs) > 2 and strs[-3] == "<|endoftext|>":
        value = 19.6
    elif tok == "</think>":
        value = 1.2
    elif tok == " " and before.endswith("\\n") and not before.endswith("\\\\n"):
        value = 1.7  # bare space after an escaped newline
    elif tok == " " and (ends_line(before) or prev in OPEN_QUOTES):
        value = 1.0
    elif tok == "." and LINE_NUMBER_DOT.search(recent + tok) is not None:
        value = 0.8
    elif tok in CLOSE_AFTER_WORD and is_word_end(prev):
        value = CLOSE_AFTER_WORD[tok]
    elif tok in LINE_BULLETS and ends_line(before):
        value = LINE_BULLETS[tok]
    else:
        value = 0.0
    return carry, value

"high-quality", "world-class", "cutting-edge", "first-class", "award-winning",
"top-notch", "entry-level", "high-end", "open source", "well-known". The first word of

    middle working next open well best entry full mid medium premium industry industrial
    enterprise commercial professional medical military consumer business food evidence
    early late highly widely internationally lesser good better great poor superior""".split()
)

    "winning": 6, "notch": 6, "class": 5, "quality": 5, "edge": 4,
    "profile": 3, "resolution": 3, "definition": 3, "grade": 3, "tech": 3,
    "income": 3, "tier": 3, "rated": 3, "regarded": 3, "leading": 3, "renowned": 3,
    "risk": 2, "source": 2, "end": 2, "generation": 2, "gen": 2, "performance": 2,
    "cost": 2, "length": 2, "size": 2, "sized": 2, "scale": 2, "rate": 2,
    "priority": 2, "looking": 2, "based": 2, "standard": 2, "standards": 2,
    "hand": 2, "aged": 2, "range": 2, "famous": 2,

def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    """Activation at this position: minus the strength of the second word if the
    previous word is a grading word, else 0."""

A short clause supplies verb families (storage, output, placement), object
pronouns, and elementary grammar. These strengthen a negative preposition
response; activity verbs and infinitive-selecting cues weaken it. Abstract
dependency 'on' is treated separately. A quarter of that
response persists onto an immediately following determiner. Smaller lexical
responses cover separation/ownership and several foreign prepositions.

Examples include 'stored in', 'printed on', and 'sent it to'.
This is a local grammatical approximation, not a parser of the whole sentence.
"""
import re
from functools import lru_cache
import wordnet

READS = ()

STORAGE = frozenset('store save record cache log archive'.split())
OUTPUT = frozenset(
    'show display print publish post render present represent list specify report'.split()
)
PLACEMENT = frozenset(
    'put place send transfer feed add insert include provide supply apply '
    'submit upload copy paste keep package'.split()
)
ACTIVITY = frozenset('work live stand reside sit stay engage participate join'.split())
INFINITIVE = frozenset(
    'want need wish hope try able unable seem appear ought used tend going '
    'supposed enough necessary important possible impossible easy difficult hard'.split()
)
OBJECTS = frozenset(
    'it them this that these those everything something anything nothing'.split()
)
DETERMINERS = frozenset(
    'a an the my your his her its our their this that these those some any '
    'another other different each every all'.split()
)
PRIMARY = frozenset('in on into onto within to as with at'.split())
SPATIAL = frozenset('in on into onto within'.split())
COPULAS = frozenset('be is are was were been being'.split())

BASE = {
    'in': -0.31,
    'on': -0.34,
    'to': -0.11,
    'into': -0.67,
    'onto': -0.37,
    'as': -0.10,
    'with': -0.02,
    'at': 0.01,
    'within': -0.12,
    'inside': -0.35,
    'via': -0.51,
    'from': -0.04,
    'through': -0.12,
    'в': -0.33,
    'на': -0.16,
    'en': -0.19,
    'em': -0.42,
    'sur': -0.41,
    'im': -0.25,
}

@lru_cache(maxsize=20000)
def word_features(word):
    forms = frozenset(wordnet.base_forms(word, 'verb'))
    past = bool(forms) and (
        word.endswith('ed') or
        (word not in forms and not word.endswith(('ing', 's')))
    )
    return (bool(forms & STORAGE), bool(forms & OUTPUT),
            bool(forms & PLACEMENT), past, bool(forms & ACTIVITY),
            word in INFINITIVE or bool(forms & INFINITIVE))


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:
        history, previous_preposition = (), 0.0

            past = True

        recent_output = any(f[1] for f in recent)
        recent_placement = any(f[2] for f in recent)

        spatial = word in SPATIAL

        if placement:
            value -= 0.31
        if past and placement:
            value -= 0.69
        if obj:
            value -= 0.60
        if storage:
            value -= 1.01
        if recent_placement:
            value -= 0.42
        if past:
            value -= 0.27
        if recent_storage:
            value -= 0.68
        if word == 'to' and past:
            value += 0.18
        if obj and recent_placement:
            value -= 0.82
        if word == 'on' and output:
            value -= 0.86
        if spatial and activity:
            value += 0.40
        if word == 'to' and infinitive:
            value += 0.17
        if recent_output:
            value -= 0.26
        if word == 'in' and last in COPULAS:
            value -= 0.38
        if past and storage:
            value -= 0.94
        # 'Based on' and 'depends on' do not describe putting an object on it.

            'base', 'depend', 'rely'

"""Destination prepositions after verbs of placing, storing, showing or recording.

What it captures: this component goes strongly negative on a preposition
('in', 'on', 'into', 'onto', 'to', 'as', ...) that introduces where or as what something
is put, stored, listed, recorded, displayed, published or provided, e.g. "stored in",
"recorded on", "put it into", "published in", "export to", "saved as", "shown in".
The negative is strongest when such a verb (or an object like "it"/"them") comes just
before the preposition, and weaker when the verb is further back in the same clause.
Elsewhere, in/on/into/to/as are weakly negative (to least), except slightly positive
after verbs of starting, continuing or working ("start to", "working in"). The word a,
an or the right after a destination preposition is mildly negative.

verb in the current clause, and the previous word. Punctuation ends a clause and
document boundaries reset it.

    """
    store stored storing recorded record records recording put putting placed place
    saved save saving published publish posted post sent send sending added add adding
    included include listed list displayed display shown show showing provided provide
    kept keep copied copy converted convert converting written write writing inserted
    insert entered enter uploaded upload exported export transferred transfer loaded load
    printed print packaged deposited archived presented present delivered deliver supplied
    supply dumped poured mixed injected inject contained tuck distributed distribute
    credited assigned assign released hosted dropped drop emailed email mailed mail
    forwarded pasted paste translate translated rendered render illustrated illustrate
    depicted featured sold collected logged implemented conveyed reported incorporated
    mapped represented indicated specified wrapped disclosed arranged accepted coated
    produced announced mounted grown fed housed stocked quoted preserved settled submitted
    embedded embed attached available
    """.split()
)

# Verbs of starting, continuing or working: a following preposition is mildly positive.
ACTIVITY = {
    "start", "started", "starts", "begin", "begins", "beginning", "continue", "continues",
    "continued", "work", "working", "worked", "hold", "stuck", "engaged",
}
# Strength of a destination preposition near a placing verb (negative activation).
NEAR = {"into": -2.0, "onto": -2.0, "in": -1.4, "on": -1.4, "as": -1.2, "to": -0.8,
        "via": -0.7, "within": -0.8, "inside": -0.6, "through": -0.6, "at": -0.5}
# Strength of the same prepositions elsewhere.
FAR = {"in": -0.35, "on": -0.35, "into": -0.6, "to": -0.1, "as": -0.15}
PUNCT = set(".,;:!?()[]{}\"'`\n")


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    # carry: (words since the last placing verb in this clause or None, previous word)
    since, prev = (None, "") if carry is None else carry

    value = 0.0
    if t in NEAR and (near or prev in OBJECTS):
        value = NEAR[t]
    elif t in NEAR and since is not None and since <= 7:
        value = 0.5 * NEAR[t]
    elif t in FAR and prev in ACTIVITY:
        value = 0.25
    elif t in FAR:
        value = FAR[t]
    elif t in ("a", "an", "the") and prev in NEAR and near:
        value = -0.3
    if t in PLACE:
        since = 0
    elif since is not None:
        since += 1
    return (since, t), float(value)

mostly silent, so they are left out: including them made the score worse.

The program predicts 0.6 on an escaped '*' or '$' and 0 everywhere else. That is roughly
the mean activation on those positions. Most of the component's variance is small diffuse
background that this does not capture, so the variance explained is small (about 0.009 on
eval); the program's main value is pointing at where the component's large activations
live."""

This component is almost always near zero. It goes negative when the text is spelling or
starting a word with the letter n, most strongly when that n is followed by an e sound.
The program predicts a fixed value per case, the mean activation of that case on training
rows:

1. A word starting "nea" or "nei" (near, nearly, neither): -2.0.
2. Any other word starting "ne" (need, never, next, net, ...), except "new" (see 5): -0.5.
3. A word fragment right after "ne" or Cyrillic "не" (Auftragne|h, BNE|F, Ne|el): -1.31.
4. A fragment starting with an e sound (e, é, è, Cyrillic е) right after a token ending
   in n or Cyrillic н (Emin|em, н|еб): -0.63.
   A fragment starting with another vowel (a, i, y, u) right after such a token
   (Pran|ay): -0.29.
5. Any other word or fragment starting with n or Cyrillic н (new, no, na, ni, nu, ...): -0.1.

Everywhere else it predicts 0. The rare, very large spikes (near -7, mostly in Greek,
Cyrillic and other non-English text) are not captured.
"""

READS = ()

NASAL = "nNнН"                                             # Latin n/N, Cyrillic н/Н
E_SOUND = "eEéÉèêëеЕэЭ"      # e, é, è, ê, ë, Cyrillic е, э
OTHER_VOWEL = "aAiIyYuUáàäíúüаиАИуУ"

NEAR = -2.0            # 1. a word starting "nea" or "nei"
START_NE = -0.5        # 2. another word starting "ne"
NE_SPLIT = -1.31       # 3. a fragment right after "ne" or "не"
N_SPLIT_E = -0.63      # 4. a fragment starting with an e sound right after n
N_SPLIT_VOWEL = -0.29  # 4. a fragment starting with another vowel right after n
START_N = -0.1         # 5. any other token starting with n


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    i = prefix.position
    if i == 0 or prefix.document_ids[i - 1] != prefix.document_ids[i]:
        return None, 0.0
    cur = prefix.token_strings[i]
    # the (up to) three characters just before this token, within this document
    before = ""
    j = i - 1
    while j >= 0 and prefix.document_ids[j] == prefix.document_ids[i] and len(before) < 3:
        before = prefix.token_strings[j] + before
        j -= 1
    before = before[-3:]
    word = cur.lstrip(" ")
    low = word.lower()
    starts_word = cur.startswith(" ") or not before[-1:].isalpha()
    if starts_word and low.startswith("ne") and not low.startswith("new"):
        return None, NEAR if low[2:3] in ("a", "i") else START_NE
    if cur.startswith(" ") or not word[:1].isalpha():
        return None, START_N if low[:1] in ("n", "н") else 0.0
    if before[-2:].lower() in ("ne", "не") or before[-2:] == " н":
        return None, NE_SPLIT
    if before[-1:] and before[-1:] in NASAL:
        if word[:1] in E_SOUND:

        if word[:1] in OTHER_VOWEL:
            return None, N_SPLIT_VOWEL
    return None, START_N if low[:1] in ("n", "н") else 0.0

The component fires on the dollar sign that opens a math span, and on LaTeX
syntax tokens (braces, ^, _, backslash commands) while the text is inside math.
It is quiet on ordinary words and numbers.

The program tracks whether we are inside a $...$ math span (a $ toggles it),
then predicts:
  - a large value on a "$" token that opens math or prices,
  - a moderate value on LaTeX syntax tokens while inside math,
  - zero otherwise.

LATEX_MARKS = set("{}^_\\")
LATEX_WORDS = {"left", "right", "frac", "sqrt"}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    in_math = carry if carry is not None else False

1. Roman numeral II / III (and lowercase ii / iii) written as a standalone token,

2. Double-a pieces: "AA", "aa", "AAAA", and words or fragments that start with "aa"

3. The first token of each document, where the activation is fixed by the token

training rows for each class.

ROMAN_PIECES = {"II", "III", "ii", "iii"}

DOUBLE_A_VALUE = 2.3    # mean activation on "aa"-initial pieces

"""Approximate pulses for click words and related consonant spellings.

Clicks, CLI fragments, and split cli/kli spellings give negative responses;
'on' immediately after a click word does too. Single-letter c/k fragments
followed by lic/lik are particularly strong. Some split ch/chl spellings,
concr/konkr, and Knuth give smaller positive responses. Transliteration lets
related spellings in other alphabets share the rules. Repeated middle dots
have a separate small negative response. This is a partial spelling-based
approximation, not a general detector of actions involving a mouse.
"""

from anyascii import anyascii

def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    first = carry is None or carry[0] != doc
    previous = '' if first else carry[1]
    current = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    p, c = anyascii(previous).lower(), anyascii(current).lower()
    joined, boundary = p[-24:] + c, len(p[-24:])

    def split(pattern):
        """The spelling must straddle the newest token boundary."""
        return any(m.start() < boundary < m.end()
                   for m in re.finditer(pattern, joined))

    click = bool(re.search(r'click(?:s|ed|ing)?$', c))
    value = -0.0007
    if click:
        value -= 1.50
        value -= 2.07 * c.endswith('ing')
        value -= 0.73 * current[:1].isspace()
        value -= 3.02 * first
        value -= 3.55 * (p.strip() in ('right', 'double'))
    if c.strip() == 'on' and re.search(r'click(?:s|ed|ing)?$', p):
        value -= 4.37
    if re.search(r'(?:^|[ /\.])cli$', c) and not current.strip().isupper():
        value -= 1.94
    if '点击' in current or 'クリック' in current:
        value -= 2.27

    # Newly completed consonant clusters, rather than whole ordinary words.
    value -= 0.76 * split(r'[ck]li[ck]')
    value -= 0.45 * split(r'[bgp]li[ckq]')
    if not re.search(r'[ck]li[ck]', joined):
        value -= 0.43 * split(r'[ck]li')
    if re.search(r'[ck]$', p) and re.match(r'li[ck]', c):
        value -= 0.85
        if re.search(r'(?:^|\W)[ck]$', p):
            value -= 6.05
    if p.endswith('bb') and re.match(r'lic', c):
        value -= 0.48
        value -= 2.45 * (c == 'lic')
    value -= 1.84 * split(r'clap')
    value -= 1.43 * split(r'[ck]r[iy][ck]')
    value -= 1.88 * split(r'sk[iy][ck]')

    # Opposite-sign spelling responses.
    if not split(r'clap'):
        value += 0.37 * split(r'[ck]l[ae]')
    value += 0.49 * split(r'nech')
    value += 2.99 * split(r'concr|konkr')
    value += 3.58 * split(r'knuth')
    if p.endswith('ch'):
        value += 0.87 * bool(re.match(r'l[ae]', c))
        value += 1.81 * (c == 'l')
    if re.search(r'[lnr][aeou]$', p):
        value += 1.13 * bool(re.fullmatch(r'ch(?:t(?:en|er|s|e)?|en|er)?', c))
    if len(p.strip()) <= 4 and re.search(r'[aeou][nl]$', p):
        value += 0.81 * bool(re.fullmatch(r'ch(?:t(?:en|er|s|e)?|o)?', c))
    if len(current) > 1 and set(current) == {'·'}:
        value -= 0.73
    return (doc, current), float(value)

the English UI verb "click" (click, Click, clicking, clicked, clicks), and more negative

boundary. A token without a leading space continues the word before it.

rule captures the big negative spikes; the component's many small positive and negative

READS = ()

CLICK_VERBS = {"click", "clicks", "clicking", "clicked"}
CLICK_VALUE = -2.5       # the click verb itself
CLICKISH_VALUE = -0.6    # other words containing click/lick (onclick, clickhouse...)
ON_AFTER_CLICK = -5.5    # " on" right after a click verb
HERE_AFTER_CLICK = -0.6  # " here" right after a click verb

_LETTERS_AT_END = re.compile(r"[^\W\d_]+$")


def _letters_at_end(text):
    """The run of letters at the end of text, lower-cased ('' if none)."""
    m = _LETTERS_AT_END.search(text.lower())
    return m.group(0) if m else ""

    tok = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    new_doc = len(prefix.document_ids) < 2 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]
    # the word that ends just before this token ('' if none)
    before = "" if (carry is None or new_doc) else carry

    # a token of letters only, with no leading space, continues the word before it
    if tok.isalpha() and not tok[0].isspace():
        word = before + tok.lower()
    else:
        word = _letters_at_end(tok)

    bare = tok.strip().lower()
    if word in CLICK_VERBS:
        value = CLICK_VALUE
    elif "click" in word or "lick" in word:
        value = CLICKISH_VALUE
    elif before in CLICK_VERBS and bare == "on":
        value = ON_AFTER_CLICK
    elif before in CLICK_VERBS and bare == "here":
        value = HERE_AFTER_CLICK
    else:
        value = 0.0
    return word, value

What it does, in plain terms: it reacts to a few spellings. It goes strongly negative on the
Chinese character 白 ("white", as in 白色, 白天, 明白), and negative on Latin word fragments
built from b-a-l or a-l-a ("Bal", "bald", "Bali", "ala", "ald", "alm") and on the piece "ai".
It is weakly positive on "-al" pieces after r, c, s or x ("ral", "cal", "sal", "alf").
Everything else is predicted as 0. The values are the mean activations on training rows.

The predictor reads only the newest token of the prefix, so it carries no state. It explains
only a small part of the component's variance (the component is spread across many tokens),
but it captures its strongest and most consistent triggers.

# 白 on its own: the one strong, consistent trigger (mean about -4.35).
WHITE = "白"

# Compounds containing 白, such as 明白 and 白天 (mean about -1.05).
WHITE_COMPOUND = -1.05

# Fragments spelled b-a-l, like "Bal", "bald", "Bali", "Baltic" (mean about -1.1).
BAL_FRAGMENTS = {"bal", "Bal", " bal", " Bal", "bald", " bald", "Bali", " Bali", "Baltic", "balk"}

# Fragments spelled a-l-a / a-l-d / a-l-m, and "ai" and "acc" (mean about -0.5 to -0.85).
ALA_FRAGMENTS = {"ala", "ald", "alm", "aled", "alan", "aler", "alah", "acc"}
AI_FRAGMENT = "ai"

# "-al" pieces that close an English-looking word after r, c, s, x (mean about +0.35).
POSITIVE_FRAGMENTS = {"ral", "cal", "sal", "alf", "alc", "osal"}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    if token == WHITE:
        value = -4.35
    elif WHITE in token:
        value = WHITE_COMPOUND
    elif token in BAL_FRAGMENTS:
        value = -1.1
    elif token in ALA_FRAGMENTS:
        value = -0.85
    elif token == AI_FRAGMENT:
        value = -0.5
    elif token in POSITIVE_FRAGMENTS:
        value = 0.35
    else:
        value = 0.0
    return carry, value

"""Age-word detector for layers.1.mlp.down_proj:3300.

The component fires on the word that states how old someone is. In English that is "old"
or "-old" after an age ("a 6-year-old", "76 years old"), and "age" or "ages" in "at the age
of 9", "of all ages". Other languages count age with a unit word after the number: 岁, 歲,
歳, 세, 살, tuổi. The program gives each such word a strength from a small table, raised
when a number or a span of years comes just before it. It also gives a weaker value to the
"Age" column headers, and to a few era and generation words (世纪, 世, 龄, 年龄).
Everything else is 0, which is close to the component's typical value.
"""
READS = ()

NUMBER_WORDS = {"one", "two", "three", "four", "five", "six", "seven", "eight", "nine", "ten",
    "eleven", "twelve", "twenty", "thirty", "forty", "fifty", "sixty", "seventy", "eighty", "ninety"}
TIME_WORDS = {"year", "years", "month", "months", "week", "weeks"}
# words before "age" or "ages" that make it the age of a person ("at the age", "of all ages")
AGE_OF_PERSON = {"the", "at", "of", "all", "certain", "same", "different", "that", "this", "any"}
# words before "age" that make it an era or a stage ("golden age", "young age")
NOT_AGE = {"young", "golden", "an", "great", "old"}
# age-counter words in other languages, with typical strength; the last few are era/generation
# or "age" nouns (20世纪, 年龄) that fire more weakly
AGE_COUNTERS = {"岁": 9.5, "周岁": 7.5, "岁的": 7.0, "歲": 10.0, "歳": 7.4, "세": 5.5,
    " 세": 3.5, " tuổi": 5.0, "살": 4.0, " 살": 1.7, "龄": 0.9, "年龄": 0.6, "世": 1.3, "世纪": 1.2}


def _is_quantity(s):
    w = s.strip().lstrip("-").lower()
    return any(c.isdigit() for c in w) or w in NUMBER_WORDS


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    strs = prefix.token_strings
    word = strs[-1]
    if word in AGE_COUNTERS:
        return carry, AGE_COUNTERS[word]
    prev = strs[-2].strip().lstrip("-").lower() if len(strs) > 1 else ""
    quantity = any(_is_quantity(s) for s in strs[-4:-1])
    if word == "-old":
        return carry, 3.8                              # "a 6-year-old"
    if word == " old":
        # "76 years old": the age follows a time span after a number
        return carry, 5.5 if prev in TIME_WORDS and quantity else 0.1
    if word in (" age", " ages"):
        if prev in NOT_AGE:
            return carry, -0.5
        strong = 3.0 if word == " age" else 3.5
        return carry, strong if (prev in AGE_OF_PERSON or quantity) else 1.0
    if word in ("Age", " Age", " AGE"):
        return carry, 1.2                              # "Age 9" headers
    return carry, 0.0

"""English -en word formation, contrasted with stative property phrases.

The largest negative responses mark adjective-derived change-of-state verbs
such as widen, soften and shorten.  Completing a split stem responds more
strongly than reading a whole-word token.  WordNet recognizes the bases,
including noun-derived size verbs such as lengthen and strengthen.
Slow down and other change-of-state particles are negative; stative property
complements such as straight up and short of are positive.  Word-specific
responses in unfamiliar names and identifiers are not memorized.
"""
import re
from functools import lru_cache
import wordnet

READS = ()
TAIL = re.compile(r'[A-Za-z]+$')
EN = re.compile(r'(.+?en)(s|ed|ing|er|ers)?$')

# Responses to a whole-word token and to a split ending, respectively.
EN_RESPONSE = {
    'adjective': (-5.161, -7.966),
    'size_noun': (-4.657, -7.757),
    'other_noun': (-0.371, -6.129),
}
# These three common verbs have weaker responses than the class average.
VERB_ADJUSTMENT = {
    'fasten': 2.803, 'flatten': 2.873, 'worsen': 3.902,
}

@lru_cache(maxsize=8192)
def en_class(stem):
    # Require a verb lemma: this excludes irregular forms such as 'taken'.
    if stem not in wordnet.base_forms(stem, 'verb'):
        return ''
    if stem in ('lengthen', 'heighten', 'strengthen'):
        return 'size_noun'
    if stem in ('threaten', 'frighten', 'hearten', 'hasten'):
        return 'other_noun'
    if stem in ('awaken', 'liken'):
        return ''
    root = stem[:-2]
    roots = [root, root + 'e']
    if len(root) > 2 and root[-1] == root[-2]:
        roots.append(root[:-1])  # fatten -> fat, redden -> red
    if any('adjective' in wordnet.parts_of_speech(r) for r in roots):
        return 'adjective'
    return ''


@lru_cache(maxsize=8192)
def base_forms(word, pos):
    return frozenset((word, *wordnet.base_forms(word, pos)))


# Scalar properties, positions and conditions that take stative complements.
PROPERTIES = frozenset('''
short long wide narrow deep high low hard soft strong weak straight flat
bright dark light heavy full empty free clear far near early late young old
large small good bad well poor dead fresh keen fond afraid devoid shy
rid right left
'''.split())
PREPOSITIONS = frozenset(('of', 'on', 'off', 'in', 'out', 'up', 'down',
                          'over', 'by', 'to', 'away', 'with'))
CHANGE_PARTICLES = {
    'up': frozenset(('speed', 'heat', 'warm', 'wake', 'open')),
    'down': frozenset(('cool', 'shut', 'narrow')),
    'out': frozenset(('smooth', 'black')),
}

def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    prior = carry[1] if carry is not None and carry[0] == doc else ''
    s = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    m = TAIL.search(s)
    continuing = bool(m and m.start() == 0)
    raw = m.group() if m else ''
    # Treat CamelCase boundaries as word boundaries, even inside a token.
    camel = re.split(r'(?<=[a-z])(?=[A-Z])', raw)
    if len(camel) > 1 or (prior and raw[:1].isupper() and not raw.isupper()):
        raw, continuing = camel[-1], False
    word = (prior if continuing else '') + raw.lower()
    before = len(prior) if continuing else 0
    value = -0.003
    match = EN.fullmatch(word)
    if match:
        stem = match[1]
        kind = en_class(stem)
        if kind and before < len(stem):
            value += EN_RESPONSE[kind][bool(before)]
            value += VERB_ADJUSTMENT.get(stem, 0.0)
        elif kind and before == len(stem):
            value -= 6.29

    particle = s.lower().strip(' -')
    if particle == 'wide':
        value += 0.713
    if particle == 'down' and 'slow' in base_forms(prior, 'verb'):
        value -= 4.328
    elif (particle in CHANGE_PARTICLES
          and base_forms(prior, 'verb') & CHANGE_PARTICLES[particle]):
        value -= 0.954
    elif (particle in PREPOSITIONS
          and base_forms(prior, 'adjective') & PROPERTIES):
        value += 0.262
        if prior == 'straight' and particle in ('up', 'out', 'off', 'on'):
            value += 3.702
        if prior == 'short' and particle == 'of':
            value += 4.463
        if prior == 'deep' and particle == 'down':
            value += 2.628
    if (prior in ('bright', 'deep', 'broad')
        and particle in ('light', 'side', 'dark')):
        value += 1.74
    previous = EN.fullmatch(prior)
    if (particle == 'of' and previous
        and en_class(previous[1]) in ('adjective', 'size_noun', 'other_noun')):
        value -= 3.031
    return (doc, word), value

"""layers.1.mlp.down_proj:3301 -- the "make it more ADJ" verb detector.

What it responds to: the last piece of a verb that turns an adjective into a verb meaning
"make (or become) more <adjective>": shorten, widen, loosen, deepen, harden, darken,
sharpen, thicken, soften, weaken, strengthen, flatten, straighten, lighten, ...
It also fires on the noun and -ing/-ed forms (hardening, fasteners, sweeteners).
The component goes strongly negative there (about -5, down to -12). Two weaker
companions: the particle after such a verb or after "slow"/"speed" ("slowing down",
"speed up"), and "of" after a change noun ("thickening of", "weakening of").
Everywhere else it is near zero.

How the program works: take the word that ends at this token (letters back to the last
non-letter; a word can be split over several tokens), and check whether it is an
adjective stem plus a verb ending. The stems are plain English adjectives, with the
final -e dropped before the ending (loose -> loosen, wide -> widen).
"""

import re

READS: tuple[str, ...] = ()

CHANGE = -5.5   # typical size on a change verb's last token
PARTICLE = -4.5  # "down"/"up" after "slow"/"speed" verbs
OF_AFTER = -3.0  # "of" after a change noun

# Adjectives (and a few nouns) that take a verb ending to mean "make more X".
STEMS = set("""
short long length strength wide broad deep bright dark hard soft loose strong weak
sharp straight flat thick thin sweet sad glad worse less tight fast fresh ripe black
white red rough stiff light sick dead fat moist quick sour dim dull smart bold smooth
""".split())

# Verb endings: -en, -ens, -ening, -ened, -ener(s), and the -den / -ten variants.
ENDINGS = ("eners", "ener", "ening", "ened", "ens", "en",
           "dening", "dened", "dens", "den", "tening", "tened", "tens", "ten")

SLOW_VERBS = {"slow", "slowing", "slowed", "slows", "speed", "speeds", "speeding", "sped"}
PARTICLES = {"up", "down"}


def _is_change_word(word):
    for ending in ENDINGS:
        if word.endswith(ending) and len(word) > len(ending):
            stem = word[: -len(ending)]
            if stem in STEMS or stem + "e" in STEMS:
                return True
    return False


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    # The last few tokens as text; the words in them, lower-cased.
    text = "".join(prefix.token_strings[-7:]).lower()
    words = re.findall(r"[a-z]+", text)
    ends_in_word = bool(re.search(r"[a-z]$", text))
    # The word this token ends (or the last word, if this token is not a letter).
    word = words[-1] if ends_in_word and words else ""
    before = words[-2] if ends_in_word and len(words) > 1 else (
        words[-1] if words and not ends_in_word else "")
    if _is_change_word(word):
        return None, CHANGE
    if word in PARTICLES and before in SLOW_VERBS:
        return None, PARTICLE
    if word == "of" and _is_change_word(before):
        return None, OF_AFTER
    return None, 0.0

"""Layer 1, MLP down-projection component 3302, as a rule about the words "on" and "over".

What it does: this component reads the phrase a word belongs to, not its meaning in
isolation. It is strongly NEGATIVE on a month name that follows "on" in a date
("...was released on [September] 27"), and weaker negative on the space that sits
between "on" and a day number or between the month and the day. It is strongly POSITIVE
on the word that finishes a fixed "on ___" phrase or a few related "over/which ___"
phrases: "on top (of)", "on time", "on to" (as in "went on to"), "on purpose", "on foot",
"on stage", "onto", "over time", "in which time / to", "on top of" (its "of" is the
strongest). A run of middle dots (leader lines) gives a small constant positive value.
Everything else is predicted as 0, which is the component's typical value.

The program needs no memory between tokens: it looks at the current word and the one or
two words before it, within the same document.
"""

READS = ()

# Month names: a date such as "on April 13".
MONTHS = {"january", "february", "march", "april", "may", "june", "july",
          "august", "september", "october", "november", "december"}

# Nouns that finish a fixed "on ___" phrase: on top, on time, on to, on purpose, on foot ...
ON_PHRASE = {"to", "top", "time", "stage", "foot", "purpose", "file", "board", "paper",
             "location", "earth", "average", "high", "strike", "campus", "site", "loan",
             "hand", "display", "video", "appeal", "air", "end", "track"}

# Words that finish "over time", "at which time", "in which to", "which point/case".
AFTER_OVER_OR_WHICH = {"time", "to", "point", "case"}

# "onto" and its relatives, as in "held onto", "turn onto".
ONTO = {"onto", "atop", "unto"}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    """Predict the component's activation at the last token of the prefix."""
    toks = prefix.token_strings
    docs = prefix.document_ids

    raw = toks[-1]                       # the token as written, spaces included
    cur = raw.strip().lower()

    def word_back(k):
        # The word k tokens back, or "" if it is in an earlier document.
        if len(toks) > k and docs[-1 - k] == docs[-1]:
            return toks[-1 - k].strip().lower()
        return ""

    prev = word_back(1)
    prev2 = word_back(2)

    value = 0.0
    if prev == "on" and cur in MONTHS:
        value = -4.0                     # "on April": the month of a date
    elif prev == "on" and raw == " ":
        value = -2.0                     # "on 13 April": the space before a date's digits
    elif raw == " " and prev in MONTHS and prev2 == "on":
        value = -1.3                     # "on April 13": the space between month and day
    elif prev == "on" and cur in ON_PHRASE:
        value = 5.0                      # "on top", "on time", "went on to", "on purpose"
    elif prev in ("over", "which") and cur in AFTER_OVER_OR_WHICH:
        value = 5.0                      # "over time", "at which time", "in which to"
    elif cur == "of" and prev == "top" and prev2 == "on":
        value = 8.0                      # "on top of"
    elif cur in ONTO:
        value = 3.0                      # "onto"
    elif raw == "··":
        value = 1.2                      # a run of middle dots (leader lines)
    return carry, value

"""Layer 1, MLP down-projection unit 3303: a "sit / sat" letter detector.

The unit goes sharply negative on the token that spells out "sit" or "sat" as a word:
" sat", " sitting", "SAT", "Sat", "sits", "sitter", German "Ersatz"/"Sitz"-style
endings, word-final "sat" as in "ICESat" or "Intelsat", and the sit-meaning words
"坐" (Chinese) and "ngồi" (Vietnamese). Words that only start with those letters
(Saturday, satellite) get a weak negative value, words that only contain them in the
middle (visit, position) an even weaker one, and everything else is 0.

The program tracks the current word across subword pieces (the letters since the last
non-letter, reset at each document start), so a word split into several tokens is read
as one word, and it predicts from what the text so far spells. It does not look ahead.
"""

import re

READS = ()

SIT_SAT_WORDS = {"sit", "sat", "sits", "sitting", "sitter", "sitters", "sitte", "sitz", "satz"}
SIT_OTHER_LANGUAGES = {"坐", "ngồi"}
TRAILING_LETTERS = re.compile(r"[^\W\d_]*$")


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    """Activation at the newest token: the word spelled so far, read as a sit/sat word."""
    word = carry or ""
    if prefix.position == 0 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]:
        word = ""
    piece = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    tail = TRAILING_LETTERS.search(piece).group(0)
    word = word + piece if tail == piece else tail
    w = word.lower()
    if w in SIT_SAT_WORDS or w in SIT_OTHER_LANGUAGES:
        value = -5.0
    elif w.endswith(("sat", "sit")):
        value = -1.0
    elif w.startswith(("sat", "sit")):
        value = -0.3
    elif "sat" in w or "sit" in w:
        value = -0.1
    else:
        value = 0.0
    return word, value

"""Component layers.1.mlp.down_proj:3304: the preposition "on".

What it does: this component is strongly negative on the English preposition "on"
(and "upon"), and on the same word in other languages (German "auf", French "sur",
Spanish "sobre"-ish, Portuguese/Italian "em"-type, Russian "на", Danish "på", Polish or
Slovak "na", Dutch "op", Arabic "على"). It is near zero on almost every other token,
including "in", "at", "to", "of" and "the". Its size is what the model writes into the
residual stream when it reads a preposition of place/support/topic, and it does not
depend on the position in the document.

Rules, in plain terms:
  * " on" / " upon" / "On" after an ordinary verb or noun ("played on", "released on",
    "put on", "posted on", "Asked on") -> strongly negative (about -2.7; "upon" ~ -3.7).
  * " on" right after a word that selects it ("based on", "depend(s|ing) on", "focus on",
    "rely on", "effect on", "impact on") -> only weakly negative (about -0.7).
  * " on" in the idiom "and so on" -> slightly positive (about +1).
  * Other-language equivalents of "on" ("auf", "sur", "na", "på", "на", "op", "على")
    -> moderately negative (about -1.8). "en", "sobre", "onto" -> weak (about -0.4).
  * Everything else -> 0.

Main program: `step` looks only at the newest token and the one before it.
"""

READS = ()

# Words that mean "on"/"upon" in English, and their typical activation.
ENGLISH_ON = {" on": -2.7, " On": -2.7, "On": -2.7, " ON": -2.7, " upon": -3.7, " Upon": -3.7, "Upon": -3.7}
# The same meaning in other languages.
OTHER_ON = {" sur", " na", " Na", " auf", " Auf", " på", " на", " На", "На", " على", " op"}
# Weaker "on"-like words.
WEAK_ON = {" en", " sobre", " onto", " pe"}
# Words that take "on" as a fixed partner, so it fires weakly.
GOVERNING = {"based", "depend", "depends", "depending", "dependent", "focus",
             "focused", "focuses", "rely", "relies", "relying", "effect", "impact", "emphasis"}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    previous = prefix.token_strings[-2] if len(prefix) > 1 else ""
    if token in ENGLISH_ON:
        if previous.strip().lower() in GOVERNING:
            return None, -0.7
        if previous == " so":
            return None, 1.0
        return None, ENGLISH_ON[token]
    if token in OTHER_ON:
        return None, -1.8
    if token in WEAK_ON:
        return None, -0.4
    return None, 0.0

"""p-82af68dd@100000 / layers.1.mlp.down_proj:3305 (layer 1 MLP down projection).

In plain terms, this component is a detector for the sound "lan"/"land" when it
sits inside a longer word, mostly a place or a name split across tokens:
"Finland" -> "land", "Westmor|land", "McL|ane", "Ortol|ans", and the same sound
written in other scripts (蘭, 兰, лан, ланд), which anyascii turns into "lan" or
"land". It fires strongly positive on those pieces. A "land" that starts a
word with a space (" Land", " lands") fires less. It also has one strong
negative partner: the clause-linking word "while" (or "whilst") in running
prose, as in ", while adhering to ...", dips well below zero. "while" at the
start of a line of code, as in "while (x)", dips only slightly. A few other
pieces ("ando", "ane", "ands") fire weakly positive. Every other token gives 0.

The program reads only the newest token and the one before it.
"""

from collections.abc import Mapping

from anyascii import anyascii

READS: tuple[str, ...] = ()

# The sound "lan"/"land", in any script, after transliteration to ASCII.
LAN_SOUND = {"lan", "land", "lands", "lane"}
# Clause-linking "while": strong negative in prose, weak in code.
WHILE_WORDS = {"while", "whilst"}
# Other word-piece endings that fire weakly.
WEAK_PIECES = {"ando", "ane", "ands"}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream: Mapping):
    cur = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    prev = prefix.token_strings[-2] if len(prefix.token_strings) > 1 else ""
    key = anyascii(cur.strip()).lower()
    spaced = cur.startswith(" ")
    if key in LAN_SOUND:
        return carry, (2.0 if spaced else 4.0)
    if key in WHILE_WORDS:
        # Code-like context: the previous token ends a line, opens a block, or is indentation.
        code_like = prev.strip() == "" or prev[-1:] in "\n;{("
        return carry, (-1.0 if code_like else -3.4)
    if key in WEAK_PIECES and not spaced:
        return carry, 1.0
    return carry, 0.0

"""Layer-1 MLP component 3308 (down_proj): a voiced "j/z" sound inside a word.

In plain terms: it responds to the sounds /dʒ/, /ʒ/ and /z/ when they sit inside a word
rather than starting one (a token with no space before it). In Latin spelling that is j or
z in a name or loanword, e.g. "Ke|j|riwal", "Ramanu|j|an", "Su|j|ata". In other scripts it
is the Katakana or Hangul syllables ji/za/zu (ジ, ズ, 지, じ) and the Arabic, Cyrillic and
Greek letters jim, zay, zhe, zeta (ج, ز, ж, ζ), which are the strongest responses.
Latin j/z pieces of a capitalised word split over several tokens get a moderate value.
Tokens that begin a word (a leading space), and other letters, stay at zero. Runs of
middle dots (leader dots) push it to about -1.2.

Each prediction is the class's average activation, a small rule rather than a fitted
curve. It reads only the current token and the tokens since the word began.
"""

import re

READS = ()

DOT_RUN = re.compile(r"·{2,}")
JZ_LATIN = re.compile(r"[jzJZ]")
JZ_OTHER = set("ζжзʒجزژ")  # Greek zeta, Cyrillic zhe/ze, IPA ezh, Arabic jim/zay/zhe
JZ_KANA = set("ジズザじずざ지자즈저주진질직")  # Katakana, Hiragana, Hangul syllables ji/zu/za...


def word_pieces(strings):
    """Tokens of the word ending at the current one: back to the last token that starts
    with a space, or to the start of the row."""
    pieces = [strings[-1]]
    i = len(strings) - 1
    while i > 0 and not pieces[0][:1].isspace() and len(pieces) < 8:
        i -= 1
        pieces.insert(0, strings[i])
    return pieces


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    strings = prefix.token_strings
    cur = strings[-1]
    if DOT_RUN.fullmatch(cur):
        return None, -1.2
    if cur[:1].isspace() or not (JZ_LATIN.search(cur) or any(c in JZ_KANA or c in JZ_OTHER for c in cur)):
        return None, 0.0
    if any(c in JZ_KANA for c in cur):
        return None, 0.8
    if any(c in JZ_OTHER for c in cur):
        return None, 0.3
    word = word_pieces(strings)
    if word[0].strip()[:1].isupper() and len(word) > 1:
        return None, 0.3
    return None, 0.05

"""layers.1.mlp.down_proj:3309 -- the "m then n" spelling detector.

What it does: this component fires on an n-like letter (n, Greek nu) when the
token just before ends in an m-like letter (m, Greek mu, Cyrillic м), so the
two letters "mn" straddle a token boundary. Examples from the data: "Huam|n" (as in
"instance of: Human" lists), "chorioam|nionitis", "Tham|nophis", "Hym|ns",
"Agamem|non", "om|nes", "gym|nasium", "пом|нить" (remember).

How strongly: it depends on how long the n-token is. A bare "n" (or Cyrillic
"н") after an m-ending token gives about 8; "n" plus one more letter about 6;
"n" plus two more about 4; longer pieces about 2.5. (Measured on training text:
bare n averages 8.3, n+1 letter 6.0, n+2 letters 4.0, longer 2.9.)

Smaller, separate cases: "mn" inside a short token ("MN", " Mn", "mn", "omn")
gives about 3; the state name "Minnesota" about 3. The first token of each
document sits slightly below zero (about -0.2). Everything else predicts 0.

The main pattern is an m|n boundary, so the simplest one-line version is:
"predict 8 when the previous token ends in m and this token is a bare n, else 0".
That version scores lower, because it misses the weaker longer pieces.
"""

READS = ()

M_LETTERS = set("mMмМμΜ")   # m-like letters: Latin, Cyrillic, Greek
N_LETTERS = set("nNнНνΝ")   # n-like letters
# strength of the m|n boundary by how many letters the n-token has
BOUNDARY = {1: 8.0, 2: 6.0, 3: 4.0}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    cur = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    prev = ""
    first_in_doc = True
    if len(prefix.token_strings) > 1 and prefix.document_ids[-2] == prefix.document_ids[-1]:
        prev = prefix.token_strings[-2]
        first_in_doc = False

    value = 0.0
    if prev[-1:] in M_LETTERS and cur[:1] in N_LETTERS:
        # the m|n boundary: strongest when the n-token is a single letter
        value = BOUNDARY.get(len(cur.strip()), 2.5)
    elif "mn" in cur.lower() and len(cur.strip()) <= 4:
        # "mn" inside a short Latin token: MN, Mn, mn, omn, damn
        value = 3.0
    elif cur.strip().lower() == "minnesota":
        value = 3.3
    elif first_in_doc:
        value = -0.2
    return carry, float(value)

Romance -eur cognates (flavour, favour, honour, etc.). Join subwords into

rules cover vowel-r fragments; factorise/factorize endings are positive.
Small morphological corrections soften derived forms. State resets at
each document boundary; no vocabulary-token lookup is used.

READS = ()

# English spelling family, stem(s) before -or/-our/-eur, response.
SPELLING_STEMS = [
    ('color', 'col|coul', -1.14),
    ('neighbor', 'neighb', -3.24),
    ('favor', 'fav', -4.32),
    ('honor', 'honn?', -4.78),
    ('flavor', 'flav', -5.86),
    ('savor', 'sav|sab', -4.82),
    ('labor', 'lab|lav', -1.18),
    ('humor', 'hum', -2.43),
    ('tumor', 'tum', -1.07),
    ('armor', 'arm', -2.16),
    ('harbor', 'harb', -3.21),
    ('rumor', 'rum', -2.11),
    ('vigor', 'vig', -3.22),
    ('rigor', 'rig', -2.77),
    ('odor', 'od', -1.00),
    ('vapor', 'vap', -2.75),
    ('valor', 'val', -1.23),
    ('candor', 'cand', -3.55),
    ('clamor', 'clam', -2.91),
    ('fervor', 'ferv', -3.78),
    ('rancor', 'ranc', -2.51),
    ('parlor', 'parl', -0.70),
    ('glamor', 'glam', -1.01),
    ('splendor', 'splend', -5.96),
    ('endeavor', 'endeav', -3.10),
    ('enamor', 'enam', -1.51),
    ('arbor', 'arb', -3.23),
    ('behavior', 'behavi', -0.99),
    ('savior', 'savi', -0.36),
]
ROOT_WEIGHT = {name: weight for name, stem, weight in SPELLING_STEMS}
ROOT = re.compile(
    "(?:" + "|".join("(?P<" + name + ">" + stem + ")"
                       for name, stem, weight in SPELLING_STEMS)
    + ")(?:ou?r|eur)"
)
SUFFIX = re.compile(
    r"^(?:s|es|ed|ing|er|ers|able|ably|ite|ites|itism|it|al|ally|ial|ous|"
    r"ously|ful|less|lesses|hood|hoods|e|i|a|os|ado|ada|ados|adas|evoli|"
    r"ecer|ear|o|i[sz](?:e|ed|es|ing|ation))?$"
)

# Subword fragments of the same r-syllables, not standalone words.
FRAGMENTS = {
    'eur': -0.97,
    'eurs': -0.21,
    'or': -0.51,
    'ora': 0.22,
    'ore': -0.46,
    'ored': -0.28,
    'ores': -0.46,
    'ori': -0.69,
    'oring': -0.17,
    'ors': -0.10,
    'ory': -0.08,
    'our': -0.47,
    'oure': -1.84,
    'oured': -0.69,
    'ours': -0.20,
    'ur': -0.17,
    'urs': -0.75,
}

def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    previous = carry[1] if carry is not None and carry[0] == doc else ""
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1].lower()
    match = re.search(r"[a-z]+$", previous + token)
    value = -0.0007

    boundary = max(0, len(previous) - match.start())
    word = match.group()

        value += FRAGMENTS[token]
        consonant = previous[-1]
        if token.startswith("or") and consonant == "t":
            value += 0.81
        if consonant == "v":
            value -= 1.58
        if consonant in 'bmvf':
            value -= 0.63
        elif consonant in 'gk':

        elif consonant in 'lr':

        elif consonant in 'dn':

        suffix = word[root.end():]

            continue
        matched_family = True
        if root.end() <= boundary:
            value -= 0.69
            break
        name = root.lastgroup
        weight = ROOT_WEIGHT[name]
        if name == "favor" and suffix.startswith("it"):
            weight = -1.82
        elif name == "favor" and suffix.startswith("ab"):
            weight = -2.58
        elif name == "neighbor" and suffix.startswith("hood"):
            weight = -0.58
        elif name == "neighbor" and suffix == "s":
            weight = -1.59
        elif name == "color" and "water" in word[:root.start()]:
            weight = -6.59
        if suffix.startswith("ous"):
